description: Express + Postgres notes API written to be correct. It has no planted vulnerabilities; every item is a scary-looking but safe pattern. Any confirmed finding that does not sit on a decoy is an 'unmatched' finding to review by hand (it may be a real, unplanned bug).

items.title: Template literal with an interpolated ORDER BY column inside db.query
items.why_safe: orderBy comes from a SORT_COLUMNS allowlist lookup with a constant fallback; every value is bound with $1/$2.

items.title: File path built from req.params
items.why_safe: The resolved path must stay inside the caller's own upload directory (startsWith(userDir + path.sep)) before it is used.

items.title: MD5 hash
items.why_safe: Used only to derive a cache validator (ETag) from size and mtime; no security property depends on it.

items.title: Math.random() in connection retry
items.why_safe: Only adds jitter to a retry delay; not used for tokens, ids or secrets.

items.title: Redirect derived from req.query.next
items.why_safe: target is passed through safeRedirect, which only allows same-site absolute paths and rejects //host, /\host and scheme URLs.

items.title: Secret literal in a test file
items.why_safe: A throwaway key used only by the unit test process; production reads JWT_SECRET from the environment and refuses to start without it.

items.title: Webhook route mounted without requireAuth
items.why_safe: Callers are not users; routes/webhooks.js verifies an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the raw body with timingSafeEqual and de-duplicates by event id.

items.title: Database URL with a password in an env file
items.why_safe: Placeholder value in an example file that is meant to be copied; the real URL comes from the environment.
